podcast.title: Film Title (1996)
podcast.body: The band is the subject of the 1996 film "Hardcore Logo," which is often referred to as a Canadian version of "Spinal Tap" but is considered to be more substantial. "Call it a Canadian version of spinal tap if you want but that's selling it short."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Headstones: In Their Own Words Part 2

podcast.title: Filmmaking Mentors
podcast.body: Directors Bruce McDonald and Calum served as mentors for Hugh Dillon during the production of "Hardcore Logo," teaching him essential filmmaking skills such as camera angles and how to learn dialogue effectively. "Bruce McDonald and Calum they didn't judge. They just corralled my energy and my talent and hardcore logo scared me."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Headstones: In Their Own Words Part 2

podcast.title: Hugh Dillon's First Sober Acting Experience
podcast.body: "Hardcore Logo" marked Hugh Dillon's first acting role while he was clean and sober. Despite this initial period of sobriety, he relapsed after the film's completion. "First thing I ever did that was my first experience was sobriety."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Headstones: In Their Own Words Part 2

podcast.title: Hugh Dillon's Role as Joe Dick
podcast.body: Hugh Dillon portrayed the frontman of the band, Joe Dick, in the "Hardcore Logo" movie, a significant early role in his acting career. "Hardcore logo, the band from the 1996 movie featuring the headstones Hugh Dylan as the Doom singer Joe Dick."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Headstones: In Their Own Words Part 2

podcast.title: Plot of the Film
podcast.body: The movie "Hardcore Logo" chronicles the reunion of a once-famous punk band, exploring dark events that unfold during their reassembly, and concludes with a shocking ending. "It tells the story of a once famous punk band called hardcore logo fronted by Joe Dick."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
